sentences: You just changed some code. Did you break anything? You should not need a second terminal, or a wall of pytest output, to find out.
Run the test under your cursor. A moment later, a mark next to it says it passed.
Now run every test in the file. One fails, and the error shows up right on the line that failed.
Open its output to read the full message, without leaving the file.
The summary lists every test and its result, so you see the whole picture at once.
Still not sure why? Put a breakpoint on the assert and debug that one test. It stops right there.
Ask the debugger for result. It is eight, not six.
So the bug is in summarize, and you found it without leaving the editor.

cards.title: Did I break anything?
cards.problem: You changed some code. Run the tests, read the failure and debug it, without a second terminal.
cards.before: Open the Testing panel, find the test in the tree, run it, then open the output panel to read the failure.
cards.after: Space n n runs the test under the cursor, Space n d debugs it. The failure shows on the line that failed.
